newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union says govt now risks five mln jobless.
newsitem.headline: German union says govt now risks five mln jobless.

text.p: IG Metall, Germany's largest trade union, said on Thursday that the Bonn government's current policies made a further rise in the country's unemployment level to five million likely.
Earlier, the Federal Labour Office reported that pan-German unemployment in January rose by more than half-a-million to a new post-war record of 4.66 million people.
Klaus Zwickel, chairman of the metal and engineering sector union, said the rise showed that an earlier government target of reducing unemployment by the year 2000 was unattainable.
"Rather than a halving of joblessness, this government is moving in the direction of five million unemployed," Zwickel said in a statement.
Zwickel said the target of halving unemployment was just propaganda that the government was using ahead of next year's general elections.

He further blamed Bonn and employer groups for having destroyed last year's "Alliance for Jobs" initiative which was supposed to have led to job creation measures in return for moderate wage demands by unions.
